name: Naturalisation (Nacionalidade Portuguesa por Naturalização)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 7 years of legal residence, counted from the date your first residence card was issued (waiting/manifestação time no longer counts). This is the new figure under Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026 — the previous requirement was 5 years for everyone.
This requires Portuguese at A2 (CIPLE) — CPLP nationals and those born in a country whose official language is Portuguese are presumed to meet this requirement.
requirements.fix_path: Take the CIPLE exam at A2, unless presumed to meet it.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a clean serious-criminal record and a declaration of adherence to democratic principles.

notes: MAJOR LIVE POLICY EVENT, the single most dramatic confirmed change across all four countries in this dataset: Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026 (in force 19 May 2026 — during the same window as this research) DOUBLED the naturalisation residence requirement, from a flat 5 years for everyone to 7 years (CPLP/EU) / 10 years (everyone else). Portugal's reputation as having one of the fastest EU citizenship paths at 5 years is now OUT OF DATE for anyone applying after 19 May 2026 — any source still describing '5-year Portuguese citizenship' is stale, and this is a much larger, more recent, and more confirmed change than any other naturalisation-timeline risk flagged elsewhere in this dataset (UK's Earned Settlement consultation and Germany's fast-track abolition are both smaller in scope or still proposals at various points). TRANSITIONAL RULE, genuinely important: applications PENDING on 19 May 2026 are decided under the OLD 5-year law — this route as encoded reflects the NEW law for anyone applying now, but historical pending cases follow different rules, a real nuance not captured in this file's forward-looking structure. The residence clock now counts from ISSUANCE OF THE RESIDENCE CARD specifically, explicitly excluding any waiting/manifestação time that used to count — another genuine tightening. Dual citizenship remains permitted. Sephardic Jewish route is fully covered in pt_ancestry_descent rather than here, since it was structurally a descent-based route, not a residence-based naturalisation path.
